front: Je voudrais parler au responsable, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-DREH par-lay oh res-pohn-SAH-bluh, seel voo PLEH]
back: I'd like to speak to the manager, please.
context: Conditional = future stem + imparfait endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient). 'Je voudrais' is the polite request par excellence.

front: Pourriez-vous m'indiquer le chemin ?
back: Could you show me the way?
context: Pouvoir → pourriez: the conditional of politeness.

front: Tu pourrais fermer la fenêtre ?
back: Could you close the window?

front: J'aimerais visiter le Japon un jour.
back: I'd love to visit Japan one day.

front: À ta place, je refuserais.
back: If I were you, I'd refuse.

front: Tu devrais te reposer.
back: You should rest.

front: Vous devriez consulter un médecin.
back: You should see a doctor.

front: Il faudrait prévenir les voisins.
back: We should warn the neighbors.
context: Falloir → faudrait = it would be necessary.

front: Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison.
pronunciation: [see zhah-veh duh lar-ZHAHN, zhah-shet-reh zün meh-ZOHN]
back: If I had money, I'd buy a house.
context: Si + imparfait, then conditional. Never the conditional right after 'si'.

front: Si tu venais, on serait contents.
back: If you came, we'd be happy.

front: Si j'étais toi, je n'hésiterais pas.
back: If I were you, I wouldn't hesitate.

front: Ce serait génial de te revoir.
back: It would be great to see you again.

front: On pourrait se retrouver au café ?
back: We could meet at the café?

front: Ça te dérangerait de m'aider ?
back: Would you mind helping me?

front: Je préférerais rester ici.
back: I'd rather stay here.

front: Il aurait dû partir plus tôt.
back: He should have left earlier.
context: Past conditional: aurais/serais + participle. 'Aurait dû' = should have.

front: J'aurais aimé être là.
back: I would have liked to be there.

front: Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu.
pronunciation: [see zhah-veh SÜ, zhuh nuh suh-reh pah vuh-NÜ]
back: If I'd known, I wouldn't have come.
context: Si + plus-que-parfait, then past conditional. A famous French catchphrase.

front: Tu aurais pu me prévenir !
back: You could have warned me!

front: Selon la presse, le ministre démissionnerait.
back: According to the press, the minister is reportedly resigning.

front: L'accident aurait fait trois blessés.
back: The accident reportedly left three people injured.

front: Il a dit qu'il viendrait.
back: He said he would come.
context: In reported speech, the future becomes the conditional ('the future in the past').

front: Je pensais que tu serais d'accord.
back: I thought you'd agree.

front: Ça me ferait plaisir de t'inviter.
back: I'd be happy to invite you.

front: Nous aimerions réserver une table pour ce soir.
pronunciation: [noo zeh-muh-RYOHN ray-zehr-vay ün TAH-bluh poor suh SWAHR]
back: We'd like to book a table for tonight.

front: Vous auriez de la monnaie ?
back: Would you have any change?
context: Polite way to ask a stranger.

front: Sans toi, je ne saurais pas quoi faire.
pronunciation: [sahn TWAH, zhuh nuh soh-reh pah kwah FEHR]
back: Without you, I wouldn't know what to do.

front: Je ne saurais vous dire.
back: I couldn't tell you.

front: Au cas où tu changerais d'avis, appelle-moi.
pronunciation: [oh kah oo tü shahn-zhuh-reh dah-VEE, ah-pel-MWAH]
back: In case you change your mind, call me.

front: Ils voudraient acheter un appartement dans le centre.
pronunciation: [eel voo-dreh tahsh-tay an nah-par-tuh-MAHN dahn luh SAHN-truh]
back: They'd like to buy an apartment in the center.

front: Il serait temps de partir.
back: It's about time we left.
context: 'Il serait temps de' = it would be time to (gentle hint).

front: On dirait qu'il va neiger.
back: It looks like it's going to snow.
context: 'On dirait que' = it looks like, it seems.

front: On dirait ta sœur sur cette photo !
pronunciation: [ohn dee-REH tah SUHR sür set foh-TOH]
back: You'd think it was your sister in this photo!

front: Je mangerais bien une pizza.
back: I could really go for a pizza.
context: Conditional + 'bien' = I'd happily…, I feel like…

front: Que ferais-tu si tu gagnais au loto ?
pronunciation: [kuh fuh-reh-TÜ see tü gan-yeh oh loh-TOH]
back: What would you do if you won the lottery?
context: A classic conversation question to practice the conditional.
